summary: Apply intersectional analysis and the Three Delays Model to maternal care barriers. Explore the five-day course and its practical outputs.
lede: Maternal health and gender analysis helps programme teams identify inequities across pregnancy, childbirth and postnatal care. Programme officers, midwives and gender specialists use intersectional analysis and the Three Delays Model to map barriers, examine care-seeking and referral pathways, and locate gaps in timely, adequate services. They review gender-responsive service choices, select equity indicators and prepare practical improvement plans.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who shape maternal care, identify access barriers or translate gender-equity commitments into service and programme decisions.
modules: WHO Labour Care Guide and Agency
Gender Integration Continuum and Workforce Equity
WHO Quality of Care and Accountability
Three Delays Model to Equity Action Plan
prerequisites: Recommended prior experience: working knowledge of maternal health services, midwifery, gender-responsive programming or public health programme delivery. No coding is required.
